newsitem.title: INDIA: India approves projects to cut sulphur in diesel.
newsitem.headline: India approves projects to cut sulphur in diesel.

text.p: The Indian government has approved proposals to set up facilities at nine refineries which would help reduce sulphur content in diesel, the Petroleum Ministry said on Thursday.
The ministry said in a statement the estimated cost to set up these facilities would amont to 55.7 billion rupees ($1,556 million).
The ministry said the Diesel Hydro-Desulphurisation (DHDS) units would be installed at Gujarat, Haldia, Mathura and Panipat refineries of the state-run Indian Oil Corporation (IOC).

The units would also be installed at Bombay and Visakhapatnam refineries of state-run Hindustan Petroleum Corporation, Bombay refinery of Bharat Petroleum Corp, Cochin Refineries Ltd and Madras Refineries Ltd.
